cases.user_message: Купил Bambu Lab P1S, печатаю PETG, стол 256x256. Хочу набить руку на полезных мелочах для дома — органайзеры для проводов, держатели для наушников под стол, подставки под зарядки. Сам моделить пока не умею. Где лучше искать готовые модели под такое и как выбирать, чтобы не нарваться на кривые файлы, которые печатаются через раз? Если пойдёт хорошо, удачные вещи буду потом допечатывать партиями и выставлять на Авито, штук по 20-30 в месяц.
cases.why_in_scope: Selling is mentioned only as an afterthought, while the explicit question is where to find reliable files. The component requires always reporting the license and flagging that NC and personal-use-only models cannot be sold (CC0/CC-BY/CC-BY-SA can), so it should surface licensing even though the user did not ask; a strong model without it tends to answer only the search/quality question. It also steers functional parts to Printables/MakerWorld and quality checks toward makes and make photos rather than downloads.
rubric: Explicitly warns that selling prints depends on the model's license and that CC-BY-NC / non-commercial or personal-use-only models cannot be sold, while CC0 and CC-BY (with attribution) permit commercial use.
Recommends concrete platforms suited to functional household parts (e.g. Printables and/or MakerWorld, with Thingiverse or a meta-search like Yeggi as secondary), not only art/miniature marketplaces.
Gives checkable quality signals for picking reliable files, such as number of makes and user make photos, documented print settings or 3MF profiles, and ratings, rather than download counts alone.

The answer is in Russian and fits the user's setup (FDM, PETG, Bambu P1S, 256x256 bed), e.g. mentions ready Bambu print profiles/3MF or PETG-specific considerations, without recommending resin-oriented sources as primary.

cases.user_message: Trying to find a replacement knob for an old Kenwood Chef A701 mixer speed control (the original cracked). I searched Thingiverse for "kenwood knob", sorted by most downloads and printed the top result in PLA on my Ender 3 V2. The D-shaft hole was way off and the model has zero comments or photos from anyone. There were like 40 more results. How should I go about finding one that actually fits instead of printing them all one by one?
cases.why_in_scope: The component says to sort Thingiverse by makes rather than downloads, to use make photos as evidence that a model actually works, and for obscure/vintage parts to fall back to Thingiverse plus meta-search (Yeggi) and Thangs' natural-language search. A strong model without it may focus only on measuring/remodeling the shaft or generic 'check comments' advice and not correct the downloads-vs-makes sorting or point to cross-platform search.
rubric: Tells the user to sort or judge by number of makes (and look for user make photos/comments confirming fit) instead of downloads, explaining that downloads do not show that anyone printed it successfully.
Suggests searching beyond Thingiverse, e.g. a meta-search engine such as Yeggi and/or Printables or Thangs, with more specific queries including the model number (A701) or part name.

Gives practical fit advice: measure the D-shaft with calipers and prefer parametric/customizable knob models (e.g. OpenSCAD/Customizer) or ones listing shaft dimensions, and/or print a small test of just the hub before the full knob.
Stays focused on finding and verifying a fitting model for FDM printing on the Ender 3 V2, without padding unrelated to the request.

checker_notes: Case 1: moved the selling plan to a trailing afterthought so the license warning is not directly prompted and the component's always-report-license rule is what makes the difference; tightened the fit-to-setup rubric item. Case 2 kept as is: in scope (makes vs downloads, meta-search), no leak, rubric facts correct.
